info.description: REST + WebSocket gateway for Fairino collaborative robots. NOTE: no endpoint here is an emergency stop. The physical E-stop is hardware only. /motion/stop is a functional stop of jog motion.
info.title: Fairino Web Services

get.description:
Service descriptor.

FWS is an API-only gateway and ships no user interface. This root exists
so a bare GET / discovers the API rather than returning 404.
What this controller can produce, and what each contains.
Download a backup bundle (tar.gz), base64-encoded.
What this controller actually supports, probed rather than assumed.
The full catalogue, filterable.

post.description:
Superseded by POST /api/v1/invoke/{name}. Open classes only.

Gates, most-refusing first: refused; not a single wire call; argument
shape; passthrough flag; unverified flag; needs a lease (refused here,
referred to /api/v1/invoke). The first three share fws/invoke.py with
the new route.

delete.description: Force-release a lease (administrative override); does not fire the watchdog.

post.description:
Compile-check without upload. Currently refuses with 501; see
LuaValidateClient.validate.

get.description:
Health of the controller's Lua validator; a refused connection
means healthy. See LuaValidateClient.probe_health.
`pidin` over the shell: processes running on the controller.

post.description: Reboot the whole controller OS. De-energises the arm.

Restart the robot application (not the OS).

Command is operator-supplied (services.shell_restart_command); FWS does
not guess a process to signal.

get.description:
Enabled services and a connect-and-handshake liveness probe of
each. Reports no credentials.

The controller's current fault, decoded to code, meaning and
what to check.
The whole decoded table, searchable.

post.description: Clear latched faults. The condition that caused them may still hold.

get.description: Audit trail of commands and state changes.

The same events as Server-Sent Events, for anything that would rather
not hold a WebSocket open (curl, a shell script, an EventSource).

post.description:
Start the loaded program.

A Lua program commands motion directly on the controller: the gateway's
jog bounds, step limits and IK pre-flight do not apply.

Stop the running program. Not lockable or confirmable, like
every stop in FWS.

get.description:
What the controller can do with a file, per kind, with
evidence. `fileType` is an opcode, not a type; see
fws/files_wire.py.

Recent compiler verdicts and the log-fetch budget, so the
rate limiting is observable.

Every saved revision of a program.

The teach pendant keeps history in a directory beside each program
(`user/force_test/*.lua`). Version content is not reachable over the
file wire (FileDownload takes a flat name); recover it from
GET /api/v1/backup/userdata. This route lists what exists.

List files.

`source=index` (default) is instant and returns what this gateway
uploaded; `source=controller` reads the real directory (~4 s, cached)
from the vendor's user-data backup, which cannot wedge anything. See
fws/files_listing.py.

delete.description: Delete a file. Reconciles the index when it has drifted.

get.description:
Fetch a file and its md5.

The md5 is what a client hands back as `if_match` on PUT.

put.description: Upload a file, and for Lua, say why if the compiler refuses it.

post.description:
Turn the force sensor on or off. Turning it off silently
removes force-based protection (guards, compliance,
insertion).

get.description: Everything the controller reports about the sensor.

The sensor's payload compensation and the robot's, side
by side. They are set by different commands and can
disagree.

put.description:
Tell the sensor what hangs below it. Confirmation
required: a wrong mass biases every force reading.

get.description:
What force-reactive motion exists, and why FWS does not run it.

Constant-force, insertion and surface finding modify how the next move
behaves; issuing the mode from the gateway and the move from a program
leaves them unsynchronised. They belong in the Lua program, next to
their moves.

post.description:
Tare the sensor. Do this with the tool hanging free and
the arm still, or contact force is baked into the offset.

get.description: Active tool (TCP) frame: which one, and its offset from the flange.

put.description:
Define a tool frame.

The tool frame is where the controller believes the working point is; a
wrong value silently shifts every later move and this gateway's own
pre-flight. Tool frames are numbered 1-15 (work object frames 0-14).
The active frame is not selected here: Fairino passes tool and
workpiece numbers with each move.

get.description: Active work object frame.

put.description:
Define a work object frame. Redefining one silently relocates
every position expressed in it.

get.description:
Gripper feedback where available. `fitted` is inferred from a
non-zero reading (an absent gripper answers with zeros).

post.description: Power up or reset the gripper. Most need this before they move.

Move the gripper to a position, with every argument bounded.

The wire order is MoveGripper(index, pos, vel, force, maxtime, block,
type, rotNum, rotVel, rotTorque). The last three belong to a rotating
gripper; they are sent as zeros because sending a rotation to a
gripper that does not rotate is not something to do by accident.

get.description: The catalogue, with each command's class and how it was derived.
What each class costs to call, and where the classes come from.

post.description:
Send one command, once, with its arguments validated first.

Checks in most-refusing order: exists, refused, callable, argument
shape, then lock and confirmation. Shape is checked before the lock,
before anything is transmitted.

put.description:
Set a digital output. Confirmation required: a DO commonly
drives a gripper, clamp or tool changer.

get.description:
Which side each name lives on: `rpc_only` cannot be called
from Lua, `lua_only` cannot be reached from the gateway.
Every place the two APIs, or the manual and itself, disagree.

What one real controller accepts, as opposed to what Fairino documented.

Measured with the upload validator (a one-line program, no motion or
execution). `absent` lists documented names that do not exist on this
firmware.

The catalogue, filterable. `section` matches the manual's
numbering as a prefix.
One function, on both sides, with every caveat attached.
The manual's own grouping -- motion, IO, welding, force, and the rest.

Prometheus exposition of the counters FWS already keeps.

Deliberately NOT on the always-open list: it carries live joint
positions, and this gateway treats live state as needing a key.

post.description:
Cartesian jog: solved backwards through IK and refused if any joint
would exceed a soft limit.

Move the TCP to an absolute pose, pre-flighted.

Every refusal below happens BEFORE anything reaches the wire.
Forward kinematics: TCP pose for a given joint configuration.

get.description:
How many motion commands remain queued. Zero with motion_done
false means the last is executing.

post.description:
Functional stop of gateway-initiated motion. NOT an emergency or protective stop.

Stops jogs (ImmStopJOG), program-space moves (StopMotion) and path runners.
Does not stop pendant motion, controller Lua programs, other LAN clients,
or passthrough commands. Always returns 200.

put.description:
Restore a point table. Overwrites taught positions; gated
like a motion command.

post.description:
Make a point table the active one. An empty name reverts
programs to their un-applied form.

Turn a list of named poses into a runnable Lua program.

Returns the source. It is deliberately NOT uploaded or run here:
generating a program is safe, and running one moves the arm, so they
stay separate calls with separate gates. Upload it with
`PUT /api/v1/programs/{name}`, check it with `.../validate`, then run
it through `/api/v1/execution/run`.

schema.title: Response Generate Api V1 Poses Program Post

put.description:
Write a pose explicitly -- from a CAD position, a calculation, or
another cell.

post.description:
Record where the arm is now.

Joints and TCP come from ONE telemetry frame, so the two
representations cannot disagree. Telemetry is used rather than the
RPC position getters because those answer `error 14` while the
controller is faulted -- which is exactly when someone is most likely
to be hand-guiding the arm around and marking positions.

get.description:
Programs uploaded through this gateway; not the controller's
directory (GetLuaList is quarantined).

post.description:
Load a program and optionally start it, with the same guards
as run: motion lock, confirmation, non-faulted controller.

Check a program's motion targets without running it.

Solves each literal motion target backwards through the controller's
kinematics against its soft limits. Read `unchecked` before trusting
`safe_to_run`: point names and computed poses cannot be checked.

get.description: Identity: model, firmware, mounting, and the sub-device versions.
Which tool and work frame the pose numbers are expressed in.

put.description:
Set payload mass. Confirmation required: payload feeds the
dynamic model and collision detection.

get.description:
Flange pose, before the tool transform (unlike /state, which
reports the TCP).

Consolidated robot state.

Motion and pose come from the 8083 stream; the rest via RPC. Telemetry
age is reported as `stale`.

Actual and commanded velocity, joint and Cartesian.

Read over XML-RPC (the SDK's state struct is the wrong shape on this
firmware). Actual vs commanded distinguishes "not moving" from "told
not to move", which the 8083 stream cannot.

Wrist force/torque from the 8083 stream at ~10 Hz.

These numbers include the tool's weight and are NOT gravity-compensated:
"RCS" is the reference coordinate system (a frame transform), not
compensation.

Per-joint torque in N·m from the stream at offset 108.
Independent of the wrist sensor (from the joint drives).

Is the controller back, and how far through booting is it?
Answers against the boot baseline, not a single ping.

post.description:
Shut the controller down. There is no remote way back;
deliberately not called restart.
